It gets a `kind` parameter instead of a second copy, and its canceler acts on the kind: a `swiftTask` canceler cancels the settling task (cooperative), a `process` canceler reports only, because `killpg(SIGKILL)` is authoritative and the body observes the end on its own schedule. That also makes the sweep test deterministic: no natural settlement can win the race, so the sweep must synthesize the terminal event with the canceler's `.stopped`.

   timestamp: 2026-08-22T18:23:56.481703+00:00
+- actor: claude-code
+  id: 01m0nbpyg7n36wj7078514jv28
+  text: |-
+    Implementation landed, TDD order kept.
+
+    RED first. `Tests/FoundationModelsRouterTests/RunPlaneTests.swift` and the `kind` parameter on `parkFakeRun` were written before the enum case. `swift build --build-tests` then failed with `type 'RunKind' has no member 'process'` at `ParkedRunFixtures.swift:121` — the missing feature, not a typo.
+
+    GREEN after. `case process` landed in `RunKind`, and every test passed.
+
+    What changed beyond the enum case:
+
+    - `RunPlane.swift`: the type doc comment said "Phase 1 ships `swiftTask` only ... the seam where the `process` (phase 2) and `mcpRequest` (phase 4) kinds land". That sentence became false the moment the case landed, so it now says phase 2 adds `process` and the seam is `mcpRequest` alone. It also states that Router owns the vocabulary and none of the machinery.
+    - `SessionMailbox.swift`: the same stale sentence stood in the actor's own doc comment, so it changed with it. The `cancel(completionToken:)` doc comment described the cooperative `swiftTask` half only; it now states both halves — `swiftTask` reports `.cancelled`, `process` reports `.stopped` after the capability's `killpg(SIGKILL)`.
+    - `ToolContext.swift`: `cancel(completionToken:)` carried the same one-half sentence, and it took the same change. Leaving one of the three behind would have left a reader two contradictory accounts of the same contract.
+    - `sweep()` itself needed no change. It already invokes each parked run's own canceler and puts the returned outcome into the synthesized terminal event.
+
+    The fixture, not a second copy. `parkFakeRun` took a `kind` parameter with `.swiftTask` as its default, so its eight existing call sites are untouched. Its canceler now switches on the kind: `swiftTask` cancels the settling task (cooperative), `process` reports only, because `killpg(SIGKILL)` belongs to the capability. That also removes a race from the sweep test — with no natural settlement possible, `sweep()` must synthesize the terminal event, so the assertion reads the canceler's `.stopped` and nothing else.
+
+    Evidence for each acceptance criterion:
+
+    - `RunKind.process` exists with a doc comment naming `killpg(SIGKILL)` and `OperationOutcome.stopped`.
+    - An unknown raw value throws `DecodingError`, as it did before. `decodingAnUnrecognizedRawValueThrowsRatherThanCrashing` feeds `"mcpRequest"` and asserts the throw.
+    - `processRunIsListedAndCancelReportsStopped` reads the parked row back with `kind == .process` and asserts `cancel(completionToken:)` reports `.reported(.stopped)`.
+    - `sweepPostsTheProcessCancelerOutcome` asserts the canceler ran once, one terminal event came back, and its outcome is `.stopped`.
+    - `grep -rn killpg Sources/` matches doc comments only. Router adds no shell code.
+
+    `swift test`: 1037 tests in 99 suites passed, plus 83 in 10 suites for the evals target. Zero failures, zero warnings. The two "known issue" lines are pre-existing `withKnownIssue` blocks in `RealModelHarness` and `BoundedWait`, untouched by this work.
